steps.label: Do Now: Trace a Sequence
steps.content:
Do Now: Trace a Sequence

A sequence runs one instruction at a time from top to bottom. When a variable is updated, work out the right side first, then store the result in the variable on the left.

1  Number <- 6
2  Number <- Number * 3
3  OUTPUT Number
Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Do Now: Trace Two Variables
steps.content:
Do Now: Trace Two Variables

Each variable has its own current value. A later instruction always uses the newest value stored in a variable, not an earlier one.

1  X <- 5
2  Y <- 2
3  X <- X + Y
4  Y <- X * 2
5  OUTPUT X
6  OUTPUT Y
Total: 4 marks

Selection and Trace Tables

Year 11, Unit 7 L2

steps.label: Trace a Simple IF/ELSE
steps.content:
Trace a Simple IF/ELSE

  • Record the input first, before testing anything.
  • Test the condition, then trace only the branch that runs.
  • A new row is only needed when a line changes a value or produces output.

steps.label: Trace a Selection Walkthrough
steps.content:
Trace a Selection Walkthrough

Open Trace Tables, select Cambridge pseudocode, then open the Walkthrough tab and choose Selection.

Instructions

  1. Read the code and predict which branch will run before pressing Step Forward.
  2. Press Step Forward once for each line that actually executes.
  3. Explain out loud why the skipped branch never gets a row.

Complete the walkthrough, then return to this lesson.

steps.label: Trace a Nested IF/ELSE
steps.content:
Trace a Nested IF/ELSE

  • A nested IF sits inside another IF's ELSE branch.
  • Test the outer condition first. Only test the inner condition if the outer one is false.
  • Once one branch matches, every remaining condition in the chain is skipped.

steps.label: Practice: Selection Foundations
steps.content:

How to complete the table

  1. Read the input shown above the code.
  2. Test the condition before filling in anything.
  3. Only add a row for a line that actually runs.
  4. Select Check Answers and correct every highlighted cell.

Complete Selection Foundations successfully, then return to the lesson.

steps.label: Check Your Understanding
steps.content:
Check Your Understanding

Questions to ask around the room:

  • When a condition is false, which branch gets traced?
  • Why does a nested IF only ever add one new row, never two?
  • In a chain of ELSE IFs, what happens once one condition matches?
  • Why is the outer condition always tested before the inner one?

steps.label: Choose the Right Operator
steps.content:
Choose the Right Operator

  • A completed trace table already tells you which branch ran.
  • Work out the comparison operator from which branch matches the input, not from guessing.
  • Every assignment line in the table needs <-. Every condition line needs a comparison operator.

steps.label: Plenary: Trace an Exam Algorithm
steps.content:
Plenary: Trace an Exam Algorithm

This algorithm checks a Value entered by the user, worth 4 marks. No place-value tables, no boxes, work it out from the code alone.

1  INPUT Value
2  IF Value >= 50 AND Value <= 100 THEN
3    Diff1 <- 100 - Value
4    Diff2 <- Value - 50
5    IF Diff1 < 1 OR Diff2 < 1 THEN
6      OUTPUT "Accept: Extreme"
7    ELSE
8      OUTPUT "Accept: Normal"
9    ENDIF
10 ELSE
11   OUTPUT "Reject: Abnormal"
12 ENDIF
Total: 4 marks

Cambridge IGCSE 0478, May/June 2021 Paper 21, Question 5(a)

steps.label: Plenary: Write an Exam Algorithm
steps.content:
Plenary: Write an Exam Algorithm

A restaurant offers a fixed-price menu. An adult meal costs $9.99 and a child meal costs $6.99. If there are 6 or more people at a table, a 15% discount applies to the total cost. Write pseudocode to input the number of adults and children, calculate the final cost, and output it. No hints this time.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478, October/November 2025 Paper 21, Question 4(a)

steps.label: Plenary: Trace a Grade Lookup
steps.content:
Plenary: Trace a Grade Lookup

This algorithm assigns an exam grade based on a score, worth 3 marks. Every ELSE branch in the chain contains another IF.

IF Score >= 70 THEN
    Grade <- "A"
ELSE
    IF Score >= 60 THEN
        Grade <- "B"
    ELSE
        IF Score >= 50 THEN
            Grade <- "C"
        ELSE
            IF Score >= 40 THEN
                Grade <- "D"
            ELSE
              IF Score >= 30 THEN
                    Grade <- "E"
              ELSE
                Grade <- "F"
              ENDIF
            ENDIF
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
ENDIF
Total: 3 marks

Algorithm from Cambridge IGCSE 0478, May/June 2021 Paper 21, Question 4
